prompt: In show.json, why is price_cents typed as integer and not number?
hint: Money travels in cents.

choices.text: Because number is not a JSON Schema type
choices.why: number is a JSON Schema type; it accepts fractions.

choices.text: So that 65.5, a fraction of a cent, is refused
choices.why: Right. integer refuses fractions that number would accept.

choices.text: Because integer also checks that the price is positive
choices.why: The sign is minimum's job; integer only refuses fractions.

choices.text: So that Ajv can store the price in less memory
choices.why: A schema says what is valid, not how it is stored.

prompt: Why is additionalProperties: false right in a schema that tests boxoffice's own answers?
hint: Look at what createOrder removes before answering.

choices.text: It makes validation faster for large answers
choices.why: Speed is not the reason; leaks are.

choices.text: Clients break when a field they do not know arrives
choices.why: That is the argument against it in a client's schema, not for it here.

choices.text: It catches a field that should never leave, such as client
choices.why: Right. boxoffice strips client from orders, and a strict schema notices if that line is lost.

choices.text: JSON Schema requires it whenever properties is used
choices.why: It is optional, and the default allows extra fields.

prompt: Match each keyword to what it says in this lesson's schemas.
hint: One of them only applies when another part matches.

pairs.right: the string must match a regular expression
the value must be one of a list
a confirmed order must carry a payment

right_distractors: the field is sent only to staff

prompt: check.mjs builds its validator with Ajv2020 and not the default Ajv class. Why?
hint: Look at the $schema line of the files.

choices.text: Ajv2020 is faster on large documents
choices.why: The choice is about the draft, not speed.

choices.text: The schemas are written in draft 2020-12
choices.why: Right. The default class reads draft-07.

choices.text: Only Ajv2020 can check the format keyword
choices.why: Formats come from ajv-formats, for either class.

choices.text: The default class cannot read from standard input
choices.why: Reading input is the script's job, not Ajv's.

prompt: The cancelled order failed check.mjs with /status must be equal to one of the allowed values. What was wrong?
hint: What do openapi.yaml and boxoffice's code say about cancelled?

choices.text: boxoffice, which should delete a cancelled order
choices.why: The contract keeps it with status cancelled; boxoffice does what it promises.

choices.text: The DELETE, which answered 204 instead of 200
choices.why: 204 is the right answer for a DELETE with nothing to send.

choices.text: Ajv, which does not know the word cancelled
choices.why: Ajv compares against the enum it was given.

choices.text: The schema: its enum missed one status
choices.why: Right. It was written from the create path only.

prompt: How many broken rules did check.mjs report for the made-up show?
hint: One line each, thanks to allErrors.

prompt: Why does check.mjs end with exit code 1 when an answer breaks the schema?
hint: Who reads an exit code?

choices.text: So a pipeline fails without reading text
choices.why: Right. The exit code is what a pipeline acts on.

choices.text: Because Node exits with 1 after printing anything
choices.why: Node exits with 0 unless told otherwise; the valid case printed and exited 0.

choices.text: So curl retries the request
choices.why: curl had already finished; the exit code is check.mjs's own.

choices.text: To tell Ajv to report every error
choices.why: allErrors does that; the exit code comes after.

prompt: Newman failed the One show test with no schema with key or ref ...2020-12/schema. What does that mean?
hint: Which drafts does Postman's validator know?

choices.text: boxoffice's answer broke the schema
choices.why: The answer was never compared; the schema itself was refused.

choices.text: The collection variable showSchema was empty
choices.why: The validator read the schema far enough to see its $schema line.

choices.text: The validator refused the 2020-12 draft
choices.why: Right. Removing the $schema line made both tests pass.

choices.text: Newman could not download the draft from json-schema.org
choices.why: Validators do not download drafts; they ship with the ones they know.

prompt: Why is REST Assured's behaviour with order.json more dangerous than Postman's with show.json?
hint: Which one told you?

choices.text: REST Assured runs slower, so failures arrive later
choices.why: Speed has nothing to do with it.

choices.text: REST Assured refused the whole schema and nothing was checked
choices.why: It checked the rules it knew; it skipped if/then without saying so.

choices.text: Postman's error was in the answer, REST Assured's in the schema
choices.why: Both were about the validator, not the answer.

choices.text: It ignored if/then silently, while Postman failed loudly
choices.why: Right. A green run hid a rule that was never enforced.

prompt: Why does the Postman collection carry the schema in a collection variable instead of reading schemas/show.json?
hint: What can a Postman script reach?

choices.text: Postman requires schemas in a minified form
choices.why: The minifying only keeps the variable on one line; any JSON text works.

choices.text: A script cannot read a file from disk
choices.why: Right. Neither in the app nor in Newman.

choices.text: Collection variables are checked faster
choices.why: Where the schema lives does not change validation speed.

choices.text: The file is written in draft 2020-12
choices.why: The draft is a separate problem; the file could not be read in any draft.

prompt: To keep the third Java test visible but not failing the run, the lesson marks it with the JUnit annotation @___.
hint: Maven reported it as skipped.

prompt: The boxoffice team wants to rename price_cents in the show. What can a schema tell them, and what can it not?
hint: A schema knows the provider, not its readers.

choices.text: It can tell them which clients read the field
choices.why: That is what a schema cannot say; contracts can.

choices.text: That the old schema breaks, not whether anybody notices
choices.why: Right. Who reads which field is outside the schema.

choices.text: Nothing, because a schema cannot describe a rename
choices.why: It describes the new shape fine; the gap is about readers.

choices.text: That the rename is safe, if the new schema validates
choices.why: A valid new schema says nothing about clients still reading the old name.

prompt: Where do consumer-driven contracts fit best?
hint: Somebody has to write each contract.

choices.text: A public API with thousands of unknown clients
choices.why: Strangers do not write contracts for you; that is where they fit worst.

choices.text: A provider with no consumers yet
choices.why: With no consumers there is nothing to drive the contract.

choices.text: Inside an organisation, among known teams
choices.why: Right. Each team can write and maintain its pact.

choices.text: Only where there is no schema
choices.why: Contracts and schemas answer different questions and live together.

prompt: Looking at the two pacts of this lesson, which changes could boxoffice make without failing any verification?
hint: Which fields does each pact mention?

choices.text: Rename price_cents to price
choices.why: Right. Neither pact reads it.

choices.text: Change id from sh-103 to a longer code
choices.why: Right. No pact reads id in the body.

choices.text: Rename seats_left to seats
choices.why: The Tickets app's pact reads seats_left.

choices.text: Send starts_at as 08/11/2026 18:00
choices.why: The Tickets app's regex demands the ISO form with an offset.

prompt: Why does the consumer test use like('O Pagador de Promessas') instead of the exact title?
hint: What does the app really depend on?

choices.text: Because Pact cannot compare strings exactly
choices.why: Pact compares exactly when no matcher is used, as for the path.

choices.text: The app needs a title that is text, not this one
choices.why: Right. The play may be renamed without breaking the contract.

choices.text: So the mock answers with a random title each time it is asked
choices.why: The mock answers the example; like only loosens the provider's check.

choices.text: Because the title contains spaces
choices.why: Spaces are ordinary text; that is not the reason.

prompt: The kiosk's consumer test passed, yet boxoffice has no venue field. Why?
hint: Who answered the kiosk's request?

choices.text: Pact's mock answered what the pact said
choices.why: Right. Only the provider verification meets the real boxoffice.

choices.text: boxoffice adds venue when a kiosk asks
choices.why: boxoffice never sends venue; the verification showed it missing.

choices.text: The like matcher accepts a missing field
choices.why: like checks the type of a field that must be there.

choices.text: PACT_DO_NOT_TRACK skipped the check
choices.why: That variable only stops usage statistics.

prompt: Put the steps of a consumer-driven contract in order, as this lesson ran them.
hint: The file is written before anybody verifies it.
items: the consumer's test describes the request and the answer it needs
the app's code runs against Pact's mock
the provider's test replays the pact against the real boxoffice
a mismatch fails the provider's build

prompt: A new boxoffice release starts sending a field called internal_notes in every order. Which check of this lesson notices first?
hint: Which check refuses fields nobody listed?

choices.text: The Tickets app's pact verification
choices.why: Pact checks only what the consumer reads; an extra field passes.

choices.text: check.mjs with order.json
choices.why: Right. additionalProperties: false refuses it.

choices.text: None: extra fields are always harmless
choices.why: A field that should never leave the server is a defect, and the strict schema catches it.

choices.text: The order status enum
choices.why: The enum checks status values, not extra fields.

prompt: Your team adds a schema check to a Java suite and every run is green on the first day. What should you do before trusting it?
hint: Green can mean "not checked".

choices.text: Run it again to make sure it is stable
choices.why: A rule that is ignored is ignored on every run.

choices.text: Add more live requests to the suite
choices.why: More answers through the same validator still miss the rule it skips.

choices.text: Switch every schema to draft 4 at once
choices.why: Rewriting schemas for one tool loses rules elsewhere; first find out what is checked.

choices.text: Feed it an answer that must fail, and see that it does
choices.why: Right. That is how the ignored if/then was found.

prompt: The kiosk team says their pact test passes, so boxoffice must support venue. How do you answer?
hint: Which side of Pact ran?

choices.text: Agree, because a passing pact test proves the provider
choices.why: The consumer side only proves the kiosk works against the mock.

choices.text: Their pact ran against a mock; verification fails
choices.why: Right. The verification is the check against the real boxoffice.

choices.text: Ask them to remove like from their pact
choices.why: like is not the problem; the field does not exist.

choices.text: Add venue to show.json so the pact passes
choices.why: Changing the schema does not make boxoffice send the field.
